question_text: Mei Ling is buying an apartment in Johor Bahru, Malaysia.

parts.text: The apartment costs RM $620\,000$ (Malaysian ringgit). On the day she pays, the exchange rate is S\$$1 = $ RM $3.45$. Find the cost of the apartment in Singapore dollars, correct to the nearest thousand dollars.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Mei Ling needs to borrow S\$$180\,000$ for 4 years. A finance company offers her two plans. $$\begin{array}{|l|l|} \hline \text{Plan P} & \text{Administrative charge of 0.8\% of the amount borrowed. Simple interest rate of 4.6\% per annum.} \\ \hline \text{Plan Q} & \text{No administrative charge. Simple interest rate of 4.75\% per annum.} \\ \hline \end{array}$$ Which plan costs her less? Show your working clearly.
parts.label: b
parts.answer: Plan P: interest + charge $= \$34\,560$; Plan Q: interest $= \$34\,200$. Plan Q costs less (by \$360).

question_text:
Priya runs a small business that 3D-prints custom desk organisers. She works from a rented workshop unit with a rectangular floor measuring 9 m by 6 m. Her printers sit on workbenches, and she sells every organiser she prints.

Her running costs are as follows.
- Electricity: $\$0.32$ per kWh
- Printing filament: $\$26$ per kg
- Packaging: $\$0.40$ per organiser
- Rent of the workshop unit: $\$1350$ per month

The table shows the number of organisers sold, the selling price of each organiser, and the electricity and filament used in each month from March to August 2025.

\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Month} & \text{Organisers sold} & \text{Price (\$ each)} & \text{Electricity (kWh)} & \text{Filament (kg)} \\
\hline
\text{Mar} & 720 & 9.50 & 1150 & 36 \\
\text{Apr} & 780 & 9.30 & 1220 & 39 \\
\text{May} & 830 & 9.10 & 1290 & 42 \\
\text{Jun} & 880 & 8.90 & 1350 & 44 \\
\text{Jul} & 920 & 8.70 & 1400 & 46 \\
\text{Aug} & 960 & 8.50 & 1450 & 48 \\
\hline
\end{array}

parts.text: Find the profit Priya made in August.
parts.label: a

parts.text: The selling price of an organiser fell every month from March to August. Give one possible reason for this.
parts.label: b
parts.answer: Any one sensible reason, e.g. more sellers offering similar organisers so she lowers her price to compete; she lowers the price to attract more customers and sell more; demand for each organiser has weakened; she gives discounts for larger orders.

parts.text:
Priya wants to rearrange the workshop for September so that her revenue is as large as possible.

Each workbench has a rectangular top measuring 1.6 m by 0.8 m and holds 4 printers. At full output, each printer makes 45 organisers in a month.

All the workbenches must face the same way, with their sides parallel to the walls of the workshop. For safe movement, there must be a clear gap of at least 0.6 m between any workbench and a wall, and at least 0.6 m between any two workbenches.

The workshop has a single ventilation system and a limited power supply, so the output depends on the number of workbenches in use.
- With 7 workbenches or fewer, every printer runs at full output.
- With 8 or more workbenches, heat builds up and every printer runs at only 80% of full output.
- Each workbench after the 9th has to share a power circuit, so the printers on it run at only 60% of full output instead of 80%.

Assume that the selling price in September is the same as in August and that every organiser printed is sold.

Decide how many workbenches Priya should use in September. Support your answer with calculations that take into account both the space in the workshop and the limits on output.
parts.label: c
parts.answer: 12 workbenches. At most 12 fit (6 by 2, with the 0.8 m sides along the 9 m wall). 12 workbenches give 1620 organisers, revenue $\$13\,770$, which is more than 7 workbenches at full output (1260 organisers, $\$10\,710$).

Some corresponding values of $x$ and $y$, correct to one decimal place where necessary, are shown in the table.

x & 1 & 1.5 & 2 & 2.5 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 & 7 \\

y & 8.5 & 4.3 & 3 & 2.5 & 2.4 & 2.5 & p & 3.2 & 3.7 \\

\end{array}

parts.text: Using the grid provided, plot the points from the table and join them with a smooth curve for $1 \le x \le 7$.

\hline

parts.text: Write down the total number of tiles, $S_n$, for the next two patterns $P_5$ and $P_6$.
